title: When the Great Builder Arch'd the Skies
description: When the Great Builder Arch'd the Skies in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 24, headed “The evil of sin visible in the fall of angels and men”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When the great Bui-lder arch'd the skies, And form'd all na-ture with a word, The joy-ful che-rubs tun'd his praise, And ev-ery bend-ing throne a-dor'd.

lines: When the great Builder arch'd the skies,
And form'd all nature with a word,
The joyful cherubs tun'd his praise,
And every bending throne ador'd.
High in the midst of all the throng,
Satan, a tall archangel, sat,
Amongst the morning stars he sung 1
Till sin destroy'd his heavenly state.
'Twas sin that hurl'd him from his throne,
Grov'ling in fire the rebel lies:
"How art thou sunk in darkness down,
"Son of the morning, from the skies!" 2
And thus our two first parents stood
Till sin defil'd the happy place
They lost their garden and their God,
And ruin'd all their unborn race.
So sprung the plague from Adam's bower,
And spread destruction all abroad;
Sin, the curs'd name, that in one hour
Spoil'd six days labour of a God.
Tremble, my soul, and mourn for grief,
That such a foe should seize thy breast;
Fly to thy Lord for quick relief;
O! may he slay this treacherous guest.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
